headline: Margins compress as consumer pressure forces a guidance cut
summary_short: Flowers Foods posted Q2 net sales of $1.19 billion, down 4.0% y/y as favorable pricing/mix (+1.8%) was outweighed by a 5.8% volume decline, while diluted EPS fell $0.09 to $0.19 as higher marketing, labor, and freight costs pressured margins.
summary_long: Net sales fell 4.0% y/y to $1.19B as pricing/mix gains (+1.8%) were outweighed by a 5.8% volume decline amid a tougher consumer backdrop, higher marketing, labor, and freight costs, partly offset by moderating ingredients and lower interest expense. Adjusted EBITDA fell 19.2% to $111.3M (margin -180bp to 9.3%); net income fell 30.3% to $40.7M and diluted EPS fell $0.09 to $0.19. Management is realigning the organization and cost structure following its comprehensive review, while continuing to invest in the Nature's Own relaunch. Citing weak first-half results, FLO cut FY2026 guidance: net sales to $5.070-5.142B (from $5.163-5.267B), adjusted EBITDA to $453-481M (from $465-495M), adjusted diluted EPS to $0.75-0.85 (from $0.80-0.90). Cash rose to $52.8M from $12.1M at fiscal year-end.

drivers.explanation: CEO Ryals McMullian said macroeconomic pressure, evolving consumer purchasing behavior, and sustained competitive activity created a tougher operating environment than expected, prompting an organizational realignment and cost-structure actions.

Net sales fell as favorable pricing/mix (+1.8%) was more than offset by a 5.8% volume decline; Branded Retail volume fell 7.6% and Other-segment sales fell on inflation-pressured store-branded demand.

Production costs rose 40bp of sales on lower volumes, higher labor costs, and outside purchases; SD&A rose 160bp on higher workforce, freight, and marketing spend, partly offset by moderating ingredient costs.
Net income fell with the operating-income decline and a heavier cost base, partly offset by $1.3M lower net interest expense on lower debt balances.
Derived from the cash-flow statement: YTD operating cash flow of $241.5M exceeded capex ($44.5M), dividends ($81.0M), and net debt repayment ($70.0M), building cash versus fiscal year-end.
Long-term debt fell as the company made net debt repayments of $70.0M year-to-date per the cash-flow statement; not itemized separately by facility in the release.
